newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik president, opposition leader to meet in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Tajik president, opposition leader to meet in Iran.

text.p: Tajikistan's President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri will meet in Iran this week for talks on peace in the turbulent Central Asian country, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.

The talks, the third round of negotiations between senior officials of the Moscow-backed government and Islamist opposition leaders since December, would open in the northeastern city of Mashhad on Thursday, it added.

Tehran-based deputy opposition leader Akbar Turajonzada said the talks would cover outstanding differences between the two sides after they signed an accord in Tehran last month on repatriating thousands of refugees and people displaced by four years of bloody conflict.
"The main differences concern military issues: on how to integrate the opposition forces into the government's police, security apparatus and army," Turajonzada told Reuters.

Disagreements also remained on other key issues such as each side's quota in a Commission of National Reconciliation to be formed under accords signed by Rakhmonov and Nuri in Moscow in December, he said.

Turajonzada said the application of the earlier accords had been hampered by a two-week refugee crisis in which Tajik rebels seized 15 hostages to pressure the government to allow about 40 of their men to join them from neighbouring Afghanistan.
The opposition has condemned the action of the rebel group.
A ceasefire, also part of the Moscow accords, appears to be holding after the civil war that killed tens of thousands of people in the former Soviet republic of nearly six million.
